ahead: Route A (RANK3_SCOPE.md) is fully attempted in hunts/prime_pair_error/RANK3_ROUTE_A.md, building on hunts/prime_pair_error/RANK3_ARC_TRANSFER.md (which already reduced rank 3's U-side, unconditionally, to exactly S(N) = sum_{q=2}^{R0} mu(q)^2 sum_{b mod q, gcd(b,q)=1} T(q,b), target O_eps(N^{2+eps})). The verdict is negative but complete, not a wall: (1) no unconditional individual-modulus route exists (the only exhibited closing route for the q=1 analogue assumes RH, which is circular against this hunt's own target); (2) the averaged-in-q substitute already identified in prior work (hunts/prime_pair_error/RANK3_MEAN_VALUE_TOOLS.md, hunts/prime_pair_error/RANK3_BDH_VERIFY.md) -- the Barban-Davenport-Halberstam theorem, applied at its single endpoint t=N and summed crudely over t=1..N -- reaches O(N^{5/2}) only, exactly CHHL's GRH-conditional order, one full power of N^{1/2} short of target; (3) this attempt checked one further natural candidate (applying the multiplicative/character large sieve directly to the K_N-weighted continuum instead of pointwise-in-t) and it is strictly worse, O(N^3 log N), for a structural reason that is explained in the document, not just measured; (4) direct numerical measurement of S(N) itself (not just an ingredient of it), from the true von Mangoldt function at N up to 2,000,000 and the real R0(N) (which only reaches 32 at that scale), tracks the shape of the already-proven N^{5/2}-order ceiling and gives no empirical sign of the N^{2+eps} target -- reported with the caveat that R0 in the tens cannot rule out a different regime setting in far beyond what was computed here. Z_(q) (the fourth moment) still has no candidate tool at all, a structural obstruction from RANK3_ROUTE_D.md/RANK3_MEAN_VALUE_TOOLS.md untouched by anything here. Rank 1 (U_1 at q=1) remains the actual bottleneck of (23) regardless of rank 3's status (RANK3_SCOPE.md Section 4): closing rank 3 alone, even to target strength, would not move (23)'s total order until rank 1 is closed to comparable strength.

work.what: Search for, or attempt to construct, a mean-value theorem bounding sum_{q<=Q} sum_{chi mod q} integral_0^1 |K_N(beta) * Psi(beta,chi)|^2 dbeta -- equivalently sum_{q<=Q} phi(q) * sum_{b mod q, gcd(b,q)=1} T(q,b) -- where Psi(beta,chi) = sum_{n=1}^N Lambda(n) chi(n) e(n*beta) (Lambda = von Mangoldt function, chi ranges over Dirichlet characters mod q, e(x)=exp(2*pi*i*x)), K_N(beta) = sum_{n=1}^N e(n*beta), T(q,b) = sum_{t=1}^N Delta(t;q,b)^2 + sum_{t=1}^{N-1} [Delta(N;q,b) - Delta(t;q,b)]^2, Delta(t;q,b) = psi(t;q,b) - t/phi(q), psi(t;q,b) = sum over n<=t with n congruent to b mod q of Lambda(n), for reduced residues b mod q. The bound needed is genuinely joint in the modulus/character variable (q or chi) and the length/frequency variable (t or beta) simultaneously, at order O(Q * N^{1+epsilon}) for every fixed epsilon>0, uniformly for 2<=Q<=R0 where R0 = floor(floor(sqrt(N)/3)/log(N)). This is strictly stronger than two routes already checked and found insufficient: (a) applying the classical Barban-Davenport-Halberstam theorem (sum_{q<=Q} sum_{a mod q, gcd(a,q)=1} (psi(N;q,a)-N/phi(q))^2 << Q*N*log(N), valid uniformly for 1<=Q<=N, unconditional) at the single endpoint t=N and then summing that same bound separately over every t=1..N, which gives only O(Q*N^2*log(N)); (b) applying the multiplicative/character large sieve inequality sum_{q<=Q} sum_{chi mod q} |sum_{n=1}^N a_n*chi(n)|^2 <= (N+Q^2)*sum_{n=1}^N |a_n|^2 pointwise at each fixed beta to the sequence a_n = Lambda(n)*e(n*beta), then integrating the resulting (beta-independent) bound against |K_N(beta)|^2 dbeta, which gives only O((N+Q^2)*N*d_N) where d_N = sum_{n<=N} Lambda(n)^2 = O(N*log(N)) -- at Q of order sqrt(N)/log(N) this is O(N^3*log(N)), worse than route (a). Determine: does a theorem of the needed shape and strength exist in the literature under any name (candidates to check: a two-dimensional or hybrid large sieve; a mean-square analogue of the Elliott-Halberstam conjecture or of Bombieri-Vinogradov; a large-sieve zero-density theorem for L(s,chi) summed jointly over chi mod q for q<=Q and over height in the critical strip, of the kind underlying the proof of Bombieri-Vinogradov itself but tracking the t-dependence directly rather than via a single endpoint)? Could one be constructed unconditionally from the explicit formula for psi(t,chi) plus a zero-density estimate for Dirichlet L-functions averaged over chi and q? If no unconditional construction is found, give the most precise reachable exponent (in place of N^{1+epsilon}) and state exactly what obstruction stops going further -- for instance whether the needed strength is equivalent to, or would imply, a form of the Riemann Hypothesis for Dirichlet L-functions (the way this hunt's own target N^{2+epsilon} for E(N) would itself imply RH via CHHL's lower bound). Do not assume RH in the estimate itself. Write results only under hunts/prime_pair_error/; do not touch zeta/, ontology/, harness/, docs/, or tests/; the word 'certified' is banned anywhere under hunts/, including inside a sentence disclaiming it.
